stimulus.text: The photograph, taken on February 22, 1956, shows Rosa Parks being fingerprinted by Deputy Sheriff D. H. Lackey in Montgomery, Alabama, during the bus boycott. Parks, secretary of the Montgomery branch of the NAACP, had been arrested on December 1, 1955, for refusing to give up her bus seat to a white passenger. Black residents of Montgomery then refused to ride the city buses, walking or using carpools instead. The boycott lasted 381 days, ending on December 20, 1956, after the Supreme Court affirmed that bus segregation was unconstitutional.

stem: The boycott worked mainly through which kind of pressure?

options.text: A federal law that closed the bus company for good
options.misconception: Background from the books: no federal law closed the bus company; the boycott ended after a court ruling.

options.text: Economic pressure, since Black riders were most of the bus company's customers
A state law that banned all city buses in Montgomery at once
options.misconception: Background from the books: no state law banned all buses in Montgomery.

options.text: The bus company's decision to raise fares and cut its routes
options.misconception: Background from the books: the bus company lost riders because of the boycott, not because it raised fares.

rationales.A: Background from the books: no federal law closed the bus company; the boycott ended after a court ruling.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Black riders were most of the bus company's customers, so a year without their fares hurt the company badly.
rationales.C: Background from the books: no state law banned all buses in Montgomery.
rationales.D: The bus company lost riders because of the boycott, not because it raised fares.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus says Black residents refused to ride, walking or using carpools instead, for 381 days.
2. A bus company that runs empty buses still pays its drivers and its fuel.
3. Background from the books: Black riders made up about three quarters of the bus company's customers.
4. Losing most of its fares for over a year is economic pressure, not a law closing the company.
Remember: a boycott's power is the money it withholds, not the speeches it makes.
